subject: general
question: The average of the first 50 natural numbers is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For the first **n natural numbers**, the average is always the middle term of the series.

Shortcut Formula: **Average = (n + 1) ÷ 2**

Given **n = 50**, Average = (50 + 1) ÷ 2 = 51 ÷ 2 = 25.5.

**∴ The correct answer is 25.5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** First 50 natural numbers (1, 2, 3, ..., 50).

**Formula Used:** Average = (Sum of all observations) ÷ (Total number of observations)

Sum of first n natural numbers = [n × (n + 1)] ÷ 2

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2ffa244bf6116b0b5a30e50b9b9040645167e68054941d6978b109678247551e.png] 

⇒ Sum of first 50 numbers = [50 × (50 + 1)] ÷ 2

⇒ Sum = [50 × 51] ÷ 2 = 25 × 51 = 1275

⇒ Average = Sum ÷ n = 1275 ÷ 50

⇒ Average = 25.5

**∴ The correct answer is 25.5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average of Arithmetic Progression

For any series in AP, Average = (First term + Last term) ÷ 2.

Sum of Squares

Sum of squares of first n natural numbers = [n(n + 1)(2n + 1)] ÷ 6.

Average of First n Even Numbers

The average of the first n even natural numbers is always (n + 1).

Average of First n Odd Numbers

The average of the first n odd natural numbers is exactly n.</p
